gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sulphur-point: Joystix spaces its arcade letters far apart, each stem barely distinguishable from the strokes that join it. Sulphur Point keeps a marker-like line and open gaps, so paragraphs move smoothly.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-yaldevi: Loud arcade attitude: Joystix tracks its letters widely, with curves that thin only slightly toward their ends. Yaldevi keeps its oversized lowercase and open-eyed e comfortable over many lines.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-aldrich: Junegull pinches every curve nearly shut, with no thick-thin flicker. What stands out is the closed-versus-open split, since Aldrich cups its round letters wide while the heading holds them tight.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-anek-bangla: Junegull has a signage-like plainness in every single line it draws. Anek Bangla, a sans-serif with wide, barely curled s curves, opens up generously where the heading pinches shut.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-anek-gujarati: Junegull never swells its strokes the way a pointed brush would. Anek Gujarati, a sans-serif with a gaping c and lowercase that rivals the capitals, makes paragraphs feel open and inviting.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-anek-odia: Junegull has no hairlines anywhere in its alphabet, only sturdy, uniform strokes with pinched curves. And Anek Odia, a sans-serif with unlatched rounds, supplies the open counterpoint that makes the pairing memorable.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-armata: Marker-traced and cheerfully retro, Junegull wears its pinched curves proudly. Armata, a sans-serif with generous gaps between characters and open terminals on its rounds, lets paragraphs unspool smoothly.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-cossette-texte: Retro and friendly at a glance, Junegull pinches its curves shut while Cossette Texte opens each lowercase e wide. Its large x-height keeps paragraphs comfortable to settle into.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-hind-vadodara: Junegull hunkers down, its lowercase as stout as cast iron capitals. It grabs attention with a retro, closed look, while Hind Vadodara hands over big open bowls and uniform strokes for the text itself.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-kedebideri: Junegull builds each letter from a single stroke width, pinching its curves nearly closed. Kedebideri, a sans-serif with open rounds and a skyward x-height, does the reading while the heading does the showing.
